meta.title: Ch 11: International Financial Management — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 11 (International Financial Management).

questions.q: Absolute PPP implies the exchange rate moves to offset:
questions.why: PPP ties currency movements to relative price levels; interest-rate differentials belong to IRP; both anchor IEFM models.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the model-name-to-relationship mapping AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: PPP chases the price of bread; IRP chases the price of money.

questions.q: Foreign exchange Account for Suppliers (FAS) and Credit Enablement (CEP) schemes are:
o: Export-institutional financing mechanisms relevant to FX risk of Indian exporters
questions.why: The new-syllabus IEFM content includes institutional mechanisms (EXIM lines of credit, FAS for importers? — students should recall exact current variants per study material); at MCQ level: FAS = pre-shipment finance instrument for importers — treat as knowledge of the framework.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — institutional-framework awareness is the new attempt's soft zone Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Know the plumbing of Indian trade finance: who pays whom before the vessel leaves.

questions.q: If US interest rates exceed Indian rates by 3%, covered interest parity (no arbitrage) implies the forward USD/INR premium/discount and uncovered parity's expected move are:
o: USD at forward discount ≈ 3%; USD expected to depreciate vs INR
questions.why: Higher-rate currency (USD) trades at a forward DISCOUNT ≈ interest differential; UIP then expects USD to depreciate ~3% against INR (INR appreciate). The traps are swapping direction and claiming 'risk-free profits' where the differential is exploitable only if CIP fails.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the direction-swaps in parity questions are the standard error AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Money flows to high rates only after pricing the currency's expected fade — the forward already discounts it.

questions.q: Rates: Rs 83.00/$; $1.25/£; £1 = Rs 106.00. Starting and ending in INR, the arbitrage check gives:
o: Profit via direct GBP buy only
Arbitrage profit ≈ 2.12% by INR→USD→GBP then selling GBP for INR
questions.why: Synthetic cross = 83 × 1.25 = Rs 103.75/£; market sells £ at 106 ⇒ buy £ in market? direction: convert INR→USD→GBP at 103.75, then sell GBP for INR at 106 ⇒ 2.12% gain before costs.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the cross-rate chain with direction is the IEFM computation AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Chain the cross-rate: INR/USD → USD/GBP vs quoted INR/GBP.

questions.q: An Indian borrower can take an INR loan at 11% or a USD loan at 7% with expected INR appreciation of 3.5% p.a. against USD. The effective-cost comparison says:
o: USD if expected annual rupee appreciation vs USD (3.5%) + USD rate 7% = 10.5% < INR rate 11%
questions.why: Foreign-currency debt effective cost ≈ foreign rate + home-currency appreciation (3.5%) = 10.5% vs 11% — choose the LOWER; sensitivity to FX expectations is the whole risk.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — currency-of-debt expected-cost comparison is the IEFM signature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Borrow in the currency whose interest rate times appreciation ≈ expected payment in INR.

questions.q: An Indian borrower can take an INR loan at 11% or a USD loan at 7% with expected INR appreciation of 4.5% p.a. against USD. The effective-cost comparison says:
o: USD if expected annual rupee appreciation vs USD (4.5%) + USD rate 7% = 11.5% < INR rate 11%
questions.why: Foreign-currency debt effective cost ≈ foreign rate + home-currency appreciation (4.5%) = 11.5% vs 11% — choose the LOWER; sensitivity to FX expectations is the whole risk.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — currency-of-debt expected-cost comparison is the IEFM signature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Borrow in the currency whose interest rate times appreciation ≈ expected payment in INR.

questions.q: Covered interest arbitrage requires the deviation from:
questions.why: CIAR exploits interest rate parity gaps — the forward premium/discount failing to offset the interest differential (F/S ≠ covered ratio); PPP concerns spot-price levels for goods, not the hedge calculus.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — parity of money buys; parity of rates hedges Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: PPP explains the coffee price; IRP explains the forward points.

questions.q: Export receivable of $1m in 90 days at ₹83, in 365-day ₹86-forecast terms. Which action manages the transaction exposure?
o: Do nothing and hope for spot gains
Sell the $1m forward for 90-day delivery, locking the rupee value
questions.why: Transaction exposure is the contractual-cash-in-foreign-currency gap within the deal's tenor — hedge the tenor you owe (90 days here); a 365-day hedge overlays speculation on the next year's flows, and future invoicing is a translation-irrelevant decision.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — hedge the promise, not the forecast AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Cover the check you wrote, not the bill you imagine.

questions.q: Translating a foreign subsidiary's equity under Ind AS 21 changes reported reserves; the exposure that actually matters to firm value is:
o: Economic (operating) exposure — sensitivity of cash flows to exchange rates, which need not match any accounting line
questions.why: Translation is an accounting restatement (no cash), economic is the present-value effect of currency on future cash flows — managers hedge economics; the translation line matters for covenants and ratios, which is itself a documented management concern.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the rupee line moves the books; the cash flow moves the value Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The translation loss hits the ledger; the economic loss hits the payroll.
